title: Stability Orchard: Mini-slate and Signal Bloom (Jun 2026) - Draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact release checklist + hourly rollout weeklet and a small 'signal bloom' sampler for telemetry. Intended for low-noise feature flips and small model routing changes (customer tier B -> C). Keep it short, executable by one lead + one steward on shift.

Context / scope:
- Targets: feature flag 'orchard-bloom' (gate), model routing table v2.1, and a small infra tweak to batch sizing. No schema changes.
- Risk profile: moderate — affects latency P50 for some backends and routing weights for Canary cohort.
- Objective: ship with <3% perceived latency uplift in P99 under baseline canary traffic. Restore within 30m if anomaly.

Quick roles (for the 48h window):
- Release Lead: Priya Nair (final call on go/no-go)
- Steward / Watcher: Marco Alvarez (telemetry checks + escalation)
- Rollback Executor: Eleni Papadopoulos (runbook runner - has perms)
- Communications: Samir Gupta (Slack #release-ops, incident bridge)
- On-call Eng: Jia Li (SRE)

Pre-flight checklist (complete before T-24h):
- [ ] Merge GH-PR-4321 and confirm green CI (unit + e2e smoke). Link: GH-PR-4321
- [ ] Canary config pushed to staging and a synthetic run executed (5k requests) — attach synthetic log snippet
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards cloned: 'orchard-latency', 'orchard-errors', 'routing-weight-heatmap'
- [ ] Alert thresholds reviewed and temporarily loosened/annotated with release tag (see alerts doc)
- [ ] Access and permissions validated for rollback executor (Eleni)
- [ ] Communication templates pre-loaded (Slack post, customer advisory skeleton)
- [ ] Rollback artifact prepared (previous routing table snapshot id + baked image tag)

Hour-by-hour weeklet (T0 = deployment starts) - compact calendar:
- T-24h: Final preflight sync. Quick checklist run and signoff in the release thread.
- T-6h: Quiet window begins (no other rollouts). Load baseline canary traffic to 1% of prod.
- T-1h: Start synthetic run for 30m at canary traffic, ensure no P95 regressions > 10% vs baseline.
- T0: Deploy routing table v2.1 + feature flag 'orchard-bloom' to canary cohort (1%).
- T+10m: Watcher snapshot: latency P50/P95/P99, error rate, rejected queue depth. Post snapshot into thread.
- T+30m: Increase cohort to 5% if metrics OK. Record all snapshots and note anomalies.
- T+90m: If stable, increase to 25% and run a short A/B comparison for quality regressions (sampling).
- T+3h: If stable and no customer-impact signals, open 1h window to push to 100% with 10% ramp steps every 10m.
- Post T+6h: Hold for 24h observational period.

Signal Bloom sampler (what Marco watches — rapid checklist):
- Latency: P50 (baseline), P95 (alert if +20% vs baseline), P99 (alert if +10% absolute increase in errors related to batching).
- Errors: 5xx spike > 0.5% of requests -> immediate rollback eval.
- Rejects / backpressure: queue depth increase > 2x -> pause rollouts and investigate infra throttling.
- Functional quality: sample 50 responses from canary cohort and run 'sanity' eval script (GH-PR-4321 has the harness). Report any drift in top-level eval score > 3pts.
- Cost signal: per-token time cost increase > 15% -> hold and consult Optimize team.

Rollback ladder (fastest path first):
- 1) Toggle feature flag 'orchard-bloom' off for all cohorts (safe path — instant config flip).
- 2) Re-apply previous routing table snapshot (routing-snap-20260519) via 'routingctl rollback' (10m).
- 3) If after steps 1-2 issues persist, revert infra batch-sizing commit and scale down dedicated workers.
- Post-rollback: run full synthetic (5k requests) and produce 'rollback-report' in release thread.

Release notes (internal draft for comms / customer-facing summary):
Draft internal blurb:
- Title: "Orchard Bloom: routing improvements and batch-sizing tuning"
- Short: Deployed routing table v2.1 to production to improve small-request throughput and reduce cold-KV penalty; adjusted batch-sizing defaults to reduce per-token latency variance.
- Impact: Expected to reduce mean latency for small payloads by ~6-12% in warm paths. No breaking API changes.
- Rollout plan: Gradual ramp from 1% -> 100% over 6 hours; monitoring for latency and error regressions.
- If you see issues: contact support@redwood.ai and reference release tag 'orchard-bloom-2026-06'

Open questions / risks to discuss in T-24 sync:
- Can the optimize team confirm batching-change effect on memory under 25% additional load? (Tag: @Optimize)
- Are there any customers in Canary cohort flagged for SLA sensitivity? Quick check with CS.
- Do we need to apply traffic shaping in region eu-west-1 during the 25% ramp? (Eleni to advise)

Post-release quick retro template (to be filled T+24h):
- What went well (3 bullets):
- What surprised us (2 bullets):
- Telemetry misses / gaps: (list dashboards we wish we had pre-made)
- Action items (owner + ETA): e.g., add a 'batching' chart to the main release dashboard (Jia - 2026-06-20)

Notes to self / shorthand: 
- Keep the roll window short; prefer configuration flips over image rollbacks where possible.
- Use 'signal-bloom' tag in Slack to aggregate snapshots.
- If rollback occurs, run a 1h hold with synthetic + small-customer pings before closing incident.

Attachments / artifacts to include when finalizing the doc:
- Synthetic run logs (staging) - attach file id
- Routing snapshot ids: routing-snap-20260519 (previous), routing-snap-20260609 (current)
- GH-PR-4321 checklist and harness link
- Alert config diff (pre/post release)

End of mini-slate.

-- Priya Nair (release lead)
